text:
Sean Gallagher: Dropping notes from today’s shadow-runner load test review. Looking for sign-off on alert thresholds + kill-switch semantics before we merge the alert rules.

Key data (from the load test sheet):
- 1% sampling steady-state: queue depth ~0-200, drops 0, shadow p95 ~420ms, primary p99 unchanged (<= +1ms noise)
- 5% sampling: queue depth oscillates 1k-8k depending on region, drops still 0, GPU util +6-10% in us-east
- 10% sampling (worst case): queue depth climbs to ~45k in us-east, starts dropping after ~7-9 mins when backpressure kicks in; primary p99 still ok but GPU util spiky

Proposal for alerts:
- Page: queue depth > 25k for 10m AND shadow_enabled=true
- Page: drop_rate > 1% for 5m AND shadow_enabled=true
- Ticket: shadow_error_rate > 5% for 15m (judge failures count here but not page)

Kill switch semantics question: when we flip global kill switch, do we expect queue depth to drain (worker continues consuming) or do we stop both enqueue + consume? If we stop consume, queue depth will stay high and we should suppress paging.

:eyes: pls comment esp on queue depth paging criteria + suppression conditions.

Allison Grant: Re: metrics, we should explicitly key the alerts off the control-plane flag. I don’t want a “kill switch ON but still paging because queue didn’t drain” situation.

Do we have a canonical gauge like `shadow_runner.shadow_enabled` or `shadow_traffic.enabled`? Ideally:
- 1 = shadow enqueue allowed
- 0 = enqueue blocked

Then queue-depth/drop alerts should require it == 1.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. Also note there are 2 toggles in the current implementation (per-route disable and global kill). If a single noisy route blows up queue depth, SRE response is probably “disable that route shadowing” first, not global.

So suppression condition should be “effective enabled == true”. If global kill is on OR route is disabled, we shouldn’t be paging on depth for that route.

But we still might want a global page if queue depth is massive and impacting infra even though we disabled enqueue (i.e., we’re still consuming). Different alert.

Vanessa Ortiz: From fleet angle: queue depth itself isn’t the only thing that matters; what we care about is GPU saturation and runaway load. If we’re already dropping, we’re protecting ourselves.

I’d rather page on:
- sustained drops (means we’re losing eval coverage) *and* we’re near capacity
- or queue depth growing while enqueue is still enabled (means backpressure isn’t keeping up)

But queue depth can be high during planned tests / rollouts. We should add a “shadow capacity budget mode” label? (or at least filter by env + region)

Keiko Yamamoto: On kill-switch semantics: my read of the current worker behavior is:
- kill switch blocks enqueue (gateway/policy)
- workers keep consuming existing queue until empty

That’s good because it drains without introducing more load.

Edge case: if there’s a bug and workers keep requeueing / retry-looping, depth won’t drop and we’ll still page if alert doesn’t check `enabled`.

So yes: queue alerts should be gated by enabled=true; but we should also have a separate alert for “queue not draining after kill switch” as ticket, not page.

Cole Summers: +1. Also we need to be careful with drop_rate definition. If it’s “dropped due to budget/backpressure”, that might happen at expected rates during protection. We need to separate:
- drop_due_to_budget (expected in overload)
- drop_due_to_error (bad)

For paging, I’d page on drop_due_to_error. For budget drops, I’d ticket if it stays high for too long (since it means customers aren’t getting useful shadow coverage).

Sean Gallagher: Good call. Right now telemetry is emitting `shadow_runner.drop_count` with reason tag (budget|queue_full|disabled|error). We can page only on reason=error|queue_full.

Queue depth threshold: 25k/10m was tuned from the 10% test where it crossed ~45k before dropping. We want to catch “depth rising” before we’re deep in the hole.

Allison Grant: If we’re going to use reason tags, please sanity-check cardinality. Reason is low-card OK. Region is OK. Route id is NOT OK for paging.

Also I’d prefer queue depth alert uses derivative, not absolute threshold, because baseline differs by region + throughput.

Example:
- Page if depth increasing for 10m AND depth > 10k AND enabled=true
That catches runaway growth even if peak is only 15k in eu-west.

Amara Diallo: From gateway side, kill switch is enforced before enqueue. So effective behavior is “no new shadow work.” Workers will keep pulling.

One more nuance: we have per-route kill + global kill. Per-route toggle is in policy eval path, so it’s immediate (no deploy), but there’s cache TTL (up to 30s) for route config.

So alert windows should be >= 2m to avoid flapping when someone is toggling.

Rafael Mendes: For oncall runbook simplicity:
- SEV2 page: queue depth runaway (growth + high) or queue_full drops, while enabled=true
- SEV3 ticket: judge/scoring failures, shadow execution failures (won’t impact prod response)

And suppression: if global kill switch ON, no pages except infra-level (GPU util) pages.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1. I don’t want to page the world because a PM toggled kill switch to be safe.

Also, can we add an annotation to dashboards when kill switch toggles? Helps correlate.

Sean Gallagher: Action items I’m taking:
1) Change queue depth page to “depth > 10k AND depth_slope>0 for 10m AND enabled=true” (per Allison)
2) Split drop alerts by reason:
   - Page: drop_reason in (queue_full,error) > 1% for 5m AND enabled=true
   - Ticket: drop_reason=budget > 5% for 30m AND enabled=true
3) Add ticket: “kill switch ON and queue depth not decreasing for 30m” (to catch stuck drain)
4) Confirm we have a single `shadow_traffic.effective_enabled` gauge (global+route) for alert gating. If not, we’ll add it.

If no objections by EOD I’ll greenlight the alert PR + update the runbook with these semantics.

Allison Grant: Looks good. Please make sure the alert descriptions explicitly say “Shadow-only; does not impact primary responses” to reduce panic.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: and please include the exact Grafana panels + queries in the runbook so oncall can verify “enabled state”, “depth trend”, “drop reasons” quickly.

Keiko Yamamoto: :thumbsup: also add one note: after kill switch, expect up to ~N minutes to drain depending on depth. Otherwise people will assume it’s broken.

Sean Gallagher: Yep. I’ll put a “drain time expectation” section: at current worker concurrency, 25k depth should drain in ~8-12 mins (assuming no retries). Will update once we run the next test.
